rows.abstract: Rationale: Single pregnant women must be supported and protected rather than be criticized and penalized because of their ordeal. These women need the Government's support, especially since it cannot be denied that in many cases, these women were left by their male partners, leaving them to fend for themselves unlike married women who usually have their husbands ti assist them.

rows.author: C089
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS TO SET ASIDE NOT LESS THAN THREE PERCENT (3%) OF THE TOTAL REVENUE FROM REGULAR SOURCES OF THE PRECEEDING YEAR AS LUMP SUM APPROPRIATION TO FINANCE REFORESTATION PROGRAMS AND PROJECTS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSESECTION 324 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: Rationale: Most local government units have been very deficient in coming up with and implementing reforestation programs for their respective localities. Clearly, there is lack of political will and most local officials have treated the problem ofthe fast disappearance of trees, with sheer apathy.> This bill seeks to mandate all local government units to set aside not less three percent (3%) of the total revenue from regular sources of the preceeding year for reforestation programs and projects. Setting aside at least three percent (3%) of the LGUs total revenue from regular sources of the preceeding year, ensures the LGUs ecological viability and enhances the country's resource sustainability.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2002-02-04

rows.author: C076
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING THE RIGHT TO FRANCHISEES TO DEVELOP THE RURAL AIRPORT INFRASTRUCTURE NETWORK IN THE PHILIPPINES FOR COMMERCIAL AND OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: A Rural Airport is, as used in this Act, any runway, take-off and landing are or seaway, not exceeding 1,200 meters in length, with a total land area not exceeding 20 hectares, which may be accessed by any type of aircraft rated by its manufacturersto utilize said facilities. Such airports are those that, due to their remoteness, lack the presence and continuous operations of any government regulatory body. Such an airport shall be so certified as a regular rural destination by any Franchisee.> The establishment of a private rural airport infrastructure will encourage economic activity in the hinterlands, by serving not only as transportation hubs but also as industrial, commercial and service centers which will provide countryside emplooyment to uplift the rural standards of living.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LEGISLATIVE FRANCHISES since 2002-02-05

rows.author: C076
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING CELLULAR TELEPHONE COMPANIES/MANUF ACTURERS TO PUT WARNING LABELS ON THEIR CELLULAR TELEPHONE PRODUCTS TO REMIND USERS THAT PROLONGED USE CELLULAR TELEPHONES CAN BE HAZARDOUS TO ONE'S HEALTH
rows.abstract: SEction 15, Article 2 of the 1987 Constitution states, "The State shall protect and promote the right to health of the people and instill health consciousness among them." > This bill seeks to require cellular telephone companies/manuf acturers to place warning labels on their mobile phone products before this products are sold to the public. Such mandatory requirement is a result of reports and studies showing radiation from cellular phones triggers chemical processes in the body which may bedamaging and could couse headaches, tumors and even brain cancer.

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE STATE UNIVERSITIES AND COLLEGES DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY (SUCDA) AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: There shall be established a government agency called the State Universities and Colleges Development Authority (SUCDA) for the purpose of making the operations of the SUCs more effective and efficient with quality and excellent outputs.> Rationale:This bill separates the SUCs from the Commission on Higher Education. Since 85% of the country's higher education institutions are in the hands of the private sector, the Commission on Higher Education may need to concentrate more on this aspect. There is therefore the danger that the further development of the SUCs may be neglected since public tertiary institutions constitute only 15% of the entire higher education system. The magnitude of the government outlay for the SUCs alone justifies thhe establishment of the separate agency to oversee, supervise and to maximize the returns of this investment.

rows.author: C055
rows.title_full: AN ACT GIVING CONTRACTUAL OR CASUAL EMPLOYEES HIGHER SALARY AND OTHER BENEFITS AND PRIVILEGES BEING ENJOYED BY REGULAR EMPLOYEES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Most big companies in the Philippines usually hire contractual or casual employees giving the latter a period of six (6) months or less to serve the former. Thereafter, upon the expiration of the contract these lowly will be terminated and will be rehired again after a few weeks. This practice is beind done by companies to circumvent the law on regularization of employees that an employee who has served the company for a continuous period of one year shall attain a regular status andlikewise to preclude them from extending benefits and privileges only accorded to a regular employee.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2002-02-11

rows.author: D085
rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING FEBRUARY FOUR OF EVERY YEAR AS `ARAW NG PAGDAKILA SA MGA PILIPINONG NAGBUWIS NG BUHAY NOONG DIGMAANG PILIPINO-AMERIK ANO', PROVIDING FOR SUPPORT PROGRAMS AND REQUIRING THE APPROPRIATION OF FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Rationale: The Philippine-Amer ican War began on February 4, 1899 with heavy fighting in the suburbs of Manila and officially ended in 1913, although pockets of resistance continued thereafter. This war of colonial conquest is therefore the longestwar in US history. This testifies to the courageous and indomitable spirit of the Filipino people, who fought the American colonizers and refused to be conquered even in the face of overwhelming odds.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2002-02-11

rows.author: C116
rows.title_full: AN ACT EXTENDING COLLEGE SCHOLARSHIP ASSISTANCE TO THE DEPENDENTS OF THE ACTIVE MEMBERS OF THE POLICE, MILITARY, FIRE AND JAIL BUREAU
rows.abstract: Rationale: Due to the limited budget of the government, it is unfortunate, however, that the men and women in the active service receive only meager salaries despite their devoted service to the citizenry. Constrained by their compensation, they areconsequently unable to afford a college education for their children. In recognition of the valiant service of these uniformed personnel, and in order to assist them in providing their children a tertiary education, this bill proposed that a collegescholarship assistance be extended to their dependents.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SECURITY since 2002-02-11

rows.author: D076
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8189, ENTITLED `AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A GENERAL REGISTRATION OF VOTERS, ADOPTING A SYSTEM OF CONTINUING REGISTRATION, PRESCRIBING THE PROCEDURES THEREOF AND AUTHORIZING THE APPROPRIATION OF FUNDS THEREFOR' BY DELETINGSECTION 44 THEREOF
rows.abstract: Section 44 of RA No. 8189 mandates the REASSIGNMENT of ELECTION OFFICERS to a new station every four (4) years OUTSIDE of the original congressional district they are presently serving. The affected officers claim that:  (1) it dislocates their families every four (4) years and thereafter; (2) the schooling of their children is greatly affected; (3) the reassignment entails additional expenses in maintaining and establishing a new residence in another areas every four  (4) years; and (4) beingaway from home diminishes the effectiveness of the performance of their duties and functions; etc.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SUFFRAGE AND ELECTORAL REFORMS since 2002-02-11

rows.abstract: "Youth Center Act of 2002". Rationale: These proposed Centers shall be envisioned as transient shelters, lodging facilities and skill training centers for those who are in need of immediate assistance and attention. These centers shall also serve asa one-stop youth activity center that can provide lodging, recreation facilities, and most importantly, provide livelihood and skills training, community service and voluntary work. These centers shall be treated as extension offices of the regionalof the Council for the Welfate of Children and Youth, Department of Social Welfare and Development.

rows.abstract: Rationale: This bill is introduced because it sees the necessity of creating a revolving fund for the use of the institute, the rationale behind sich a proposal being that technical/train ing personnel would then become five times more capable and productive when given the rightful additional financial backup.> The Institute can draw up funds from laboratory practicum product sales, NGO training fees, guest house and form fees, and other forms of income derived from the services of the Institute. Such revenue can further enhance the budget of AGRICULTURAL TRAINING INSTITUTE (ATI) and can additionally be used to repair and maintain existing facilities.

rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING BARANGAY NUTRITION SCHOLAR ASSIGNED TO NUTRITIONALLY DEPRESSED AREAS AN ANNUAL TRAVEL ALLOWANCE OF TWO THOUSAND FOUR HUNDRED PESOS (P2,400.00) AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NUMBERED FIFTEEN HUNDRED SIXTY- NINE, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: The Barangay Nutrition Scholar who works as a volunteer is only entitled to a meager travel allowance of P120.00 a year from the National Nutritional Council in addition to whatever counterpart fund the municipality can grant him. In economically depressed areas the Barangay Nutrition Scholar does not get any counterpart allowance from the municipality. As a result, very few volunteer to work as Barangay Nutrition Scholar.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2002-02-11

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A NATIONAL MEDICAL CHECK-UPS FOR CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASES AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Rationale:  In the Philippines, chronic rheumatic heart disease, followed by CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASES (CVD), is among the common heart-related causes of death among adult patients in general hospitals. Data at the Philippine Heart Center and the Department of Health show that the prevalence of coronary heart disease is now one among the top 5 leading causes of death in the country. > The high incidence of cardiovascular diseases has prompted the Cardiology specialists of the Philippines to propose that all persons, both children and adults undergo regular check-ups.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2002-02-11

rows.abstract: The provisions of this act shall be available to any congressional franchise holder (Franchisee) engaged in rural air transport operating any type of fixed or rotary wing, land or sea type of aircraft. > Any Franchisee may construct, manage, operateand/or maintain any rural airport in any part of the Philippines in order to eventually make each municipality regularly accessible or within easy reach of the principal and proximate urban areas with at least 100,000 population.

rows.author: D007
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING THE MAGNA CARTA FOR DAY CARE WORKERS, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: There is no law that protects the interests of one of our most important service providers. Until now Day Care Workers are only receiving a meager monthly allowance of P500 as provided for by Republic Act 6972 or the Day Care Law, a measure that rationalize the establishment of Day Care Centers in every barangay. Aside from the economic conditions that they are subjected to, Day Care Workers have no security of tenure and their appointments are in many cases subject to the whims of politicians. This is why the state should guarantee the security of tenure for these workers.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SOCIAL SERVICES since 2002-02-11

rows.abstract: This bill seeks to amend Section 13 of Presidential Decree No. 1146 as amended by RA No. 8291, otherwise known as the Revised Government Service Insurance Act of 1977. The primary objective of this measure is to allow government employees to retireafter serving the government for at least twenty (20) years regardless of the retirement age requirement under existing laws. > This measure will certainly help open windows of opportunities for prospective retirees giving them better choice in planning the future of their respective families considering the amount they will receive from retirement benefits while they are still strong and capable of venturing into other fields.

rows.abstract: "Emergency Equitable Access to Entertainment Act of 2002". A temporary moratorium is hereby declared on the apprehension, seizure and confiscation of pirated compact discs, video compact discs, and cassete and video cassete tapes in the Philippines.> The DEPARTMENT OF TRADE AND INDUSTRY (DTI) is hereby mandated to immediately undertake a comprehensive, industry-wide assessment of the pricing mechanism prevailing over the entertainment industry, in respect to production, distribution and marketing of compact discs, video compact discs and cassette and video cassette tapes in the country. rows.title_full: AN ACT EXEMPTING THE SALE AND IMPORTATION OF ALL TYPES OF AGRICULTURAL AND FISHERIES INPUTS, EQUIPMENT AND MACHINERY FROM THE COVERAGE OF THE VALUE-ADDED TAX (VAT)
rows.abstract: Rationale: Given the general weakness in the external sector, it is imperative for government to rethink its policies and seek domestic sources of growth. The agricultiral sector holds the strongest potential for the country to withstand the possible effects of a global recession in the wake of a US invasion in Afghanistan and accordingly, more incentives for our farmers and agri-based industries are in order.> This bill is geared towards that end. It seeks to exempt all types of agriculture and fisheries inputs, equipment and machinery form the coverage of the value-added tax (VAT)> It is a twin measure to another bill which provides for the exemption of the same from the payment of tariff and duties.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2002-02-18

rows.title_full: AN ACT EXEMPTING INDIVIDUALS, COOPERATIVES AND OTHER ENTERPRISES ENGAGED IN THE IMPORTATION OF ALL TYPES OF AGRICULTURE AND FISHERIES INPUTS, EQUIPMENT AND MACHINERY FROM PAYMENT OF TARIFFS AND DUTIES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NUMBEREDEIGHT THOUSAND FOUR HUNDRED THIRTY-FIVE (R.A. 8435), OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE AGRICULTURE AND FISHERIES MODERNIZATION ACT OF 1997
rows.abstract: Rationale: Considering that the agriculture sector holds the second highest multiplier effect on the national economy and as such, the strongest potential for the country to withstand the possible effects of a global recession, more incentives for our farmers and agri-based industries are in order. Removing the tax burden of the sector would be the best course of action right now to improve productivity and increase production in the countryside.

rows.author: C055
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING ARTICLE 288 OF THE LABOR CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES INCREASING THE PENALTY FOR VIOLATION OF ARTICLE 280 OF THE LABOR CODE, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: Rationale: One of the rampant abuses committed against CONTRACTURAL and CASUAL employees is refusal of most employers to acknowledge their regular status of employment after serving the company for at least one (1) year whether such service is continuous or brokern. The reason for such rampant violation is that the Labor Code of the Philippines does not specifically provide for a penal sanction for such violation. PROVIDED HOWEVER, THAT ANY EMPLOYER WHO REFUSED TO RECOGNIZE THE REGULAR STATUS OF AN EMPLOYEE UNDER THE CIRCUMSTANCES PROVIDED FOR IN ARTICLE 280 OF THIS CODE SHALL BE PUNISHED WITH A FINE OF NOT LESS THAN FIVE THOUSAND PESOS (P5,000.00) NOR MORE THAN FIFTY THOUSAND PESOS (P50,000.00, OR IMPRISONMENT OF NOT LESS THAN SIX (6) MONNTHS NOR MORE THAN SIX (6) YEARS, OR BOTH SUCH FINE AND IMPRISONMENT AT THE DISCRETION OF THE COURT.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2002-02-18

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR AN EXTENTION OF THE REGISTRATION OF MEMBERS OF THE KATIPUNAN NG MGA KABATAAN (SK) FOR THE PERIOD APRIL 8 TO APRIL 14, 2002
rows.abstract: Rationale: In connection with the scheduled May 2002 Sangguniang Kabataan Elections, a general registration was conducted last December 10-26, 2001 of members of the Katipunan ng mga Kabataan, pursuant to COMELEC Resolution No. 4713. Registration turnout was minimal. > Accordingly, the most common problems encountered were the inaccessibility of the designated registration centers which were done at the municipal or city Comelec Offices, depriving the youth living in far-flung barangays the chance to vote; and the short proximity of time between the period of information dissemination and actual inclusive dates of registration.

rows.title_full: AN ACT BROADENING THE SCOPE OF UNLAWFUL PRACTICES OF MATCHING FILIPINO WOMEN FOR MARRIAGE TO FOREIGN NATIONALS TO INCLUDE VARIOUS SCHEMES MADE AVAILABLE THROUGH THE INTERNET, AMENDING FOR THIS PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6955
rows.abstract: Rationale: In this Information Technology Age, practically any type of information can be made available for anyone with access to the worldwide web or the internet.> The Philippines is no stranger to the mail-order bride schme that exposed these schemes as another version of human trafficking. People operating these mail-order bride services market Filipino women to foreigners like one sells a price of meat. This mail-order bride scheme has not extended to the electronic technology. Thus, thebirth of the so-called electronic mail-order brides or e-mail order brides.

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8436, ENTITLED `AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE COMMISSION ON ELECTIONS TO USE AN AUTOMATED ELECTION SYSTEM IN THE MAY 11, 1998 NATIONAL OR LOCAL ELECTIONS AND IN SUBSEQUENT NATIONAL AND LOCAL ELECTORAL EXERCISES, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The enactment into law of Republic Act No. 8436 which provides for an automated system of counting and canvassing of votes is a milestone in institutionaliz ing reforms in the Philippine electoral system.  There is a need however, to amend the present law based on the lessons gained from the pilot-testing of the system particularly with respect to some legal and procedural aspects of the law.> This bill was filed by this representation during the Elevent Congress (HB No. 6261) and reported outby the Committee on Suffrage and Electoral Reforms. Other procedural and legal amendments are, likewise, introduced in this bill.

rows.title_full: AN ACT EXCLUDING THE PROCEEDS OF LIFE ANNUITY CONTRACTS FROM THE COMPUTATION OF GROSS INCOME, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE THE TAX REFORM ACT OF 1997
rows.abstract: Rationale: Statistical data reveal that a Filipino employee, in lieu of investing in fixed assets during his productive years, opts to save for the future by way of a dependable retirement plan. This includes affordable annuity products such as pension and insurance plans, which will help provide the savings facility to sustain the employee's needs  upon retirement. Thus, annuities serve as a supplementary source of income for the Filipino worker after long years of hard work. With it, the retiree can look forward to living a comfortable life. However, under RA No. 8424 or the Tax Reform Act, ANNUITIES are included among "pertinent items of gross income". This obviously puts a heavy toll on the often meager amount received by the annuitantts especially without any other source to live by.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2002-02-20
